scope: Curve and subgroup supplied, odd r, sufficiently large p for the uniform point argument. Subgroup-relative subexponential complexity applies to the stated infinite subfamily with r=p^Omega(1). Curve construction and novelty of the pairing are outside the claim.
statement: For primes p at least 11 with p congruent to 2 mod 3, the specified Weil polynomial gives an ordinary absolutely simple genus-two Jacobian isogeny class. Given a curve and a prime-order subgroup of order r dividing p−1, the classical Frey–Rück reduction yields an expected L_p(1/2,O(1)) discrete-logorithm algorithm.
